title: Mai Mercado 2016 to 2024 — Long-Tail Impact Chronology
identity_rule: The 2016 legal/prison actor is the Son. Do not expose the Son's real name or family names.
purpose: Connect the 2016 legal case, police-door intervention, imprisonment and evidence-access asymmetry to the Son's reported long-term psychological, social, political and occupational aftermath, including later retirement around 2024.
evidence_rule: Firsthand aftermath claims are high-value primary biographical evidence. Medical causation and exact retirement status/date require documentary corroboration before being stated as independently established facts.

chronology.event: Mercado publishes the initiating Christiania Facebook post using forceful rhetoric and foregrounding her newborn.
Multi-speaker Facebook conflict escalates; attribution and reply topology later become central evidentiary problems.

Police attend the Son's private home. The Son's firsthand account says officers tell him not to contact Mercado again. Exact legal status of the instruction remains unresolved: warning/admonition versus formal tilhold.

The Son sends the reciprocal consequences statement, including the reported formulation that if there are consequences for him there will also be consequences for Mercado and that it is not a threat but a guarantee.

The Son is remanded. He denies guilt, appeals remand, explains ADHD/medical-cannabis and dialogue motives, and denies intending to seek Mercado out and carry out violence. His phone/computer are under police control.

The Son remains within the criminal process while his ability to independently preserve and reconstruct the changing Facebook object is constrained. He later reports difficulty getting relevant material into the case file.
Retten i Sønderborg convicts on three of four counts and imposes five months' unconditional imprisonment.
The Son reports a major decline in trust toward police, courts, government, Danish politics and institutional authority. He increasingly avoids participation in those systems.

The Son reports reluctance to open the door when someone knocks, social withdrawal, unexplained crying, cessation of gaming, loss of ordinary pleasure, and becoming harder and more serious in social presentation.
Severe C-PTSD becomes part of the Son's own account of the long-term psychological aftermath.
The Son reports that Tim/the Son receives retirement status and effectively leaves ordinary work obligations. Exact Danish legal category and decision date remain to be confirmed.
Retirement becomes a potential objective long-tail marker of reduced work participation if records show the decision was materially connected to long-term psychiatric or functional impairment.

The 2016 case is interpreted as a major biographical rupture shaping themes of karma, reciprocity, distrust of state authority, moral versus legal legitimacy, and withdrawal from Danish institutional life.

causal_model.working_sequence: political conflict -> institutional/security escalation -> police-door intervention -> disputed later communication -> arrest/remand -> device/evidence-control asymmetry -> conviction/imprisonment -> public stigma -> institutional distrust -> social/emotional withdrawal -> possible long-term work-capacity loss -> retirement around 2024
causal_model.caution: The sequence establishes chronology and firsthand attribution, not sole medical causation. Other life events may also have contributed to later C-PTSD and work impairment.

research_targets: exact legal category of retirement benefit
medical records or diagnostic chronology where lawfully available
contemporaneous 2016-2024 messages documenting institutional distrust and withdrawal
records showing onset/worsening of trauma symptoms
testimony from people who knew the Son before and after the case
